title: introduce-cost-oracle-autosuggest-and-safeguard-defaults
author: Ivy Chen
release_notes: Introduces the Cost Oracle autosuggest CLI and safe default profiles for batching, prefill/caching, and quantization; includes migration script and docs. Backwards compatible defaults applied only when enabled.
description: Context: Customers frequently ask for conservative, production-safe defaults for batching, KV/prefix cache, and quantization that maximize unit economics without risking latency SLOs. Existing autotune pieces produce good results but are hard to simulate before applying and do not provide a simple dry-run feedback loop. This PR introduces the "Cost Oracle" — an offline simulator and autosuggest component surfaced as a CLI and lightweight Console API that generates conservative recommended defaults and a safety gate (rollbackable profiles). Motivation: reduce friction for SREs/Platform engineers to adopt cost-saving profiles, give confidence via a deterministic dry-run cost/latency simulation, and provide an audit-friendly change artifact. What this PR does (summary): - Adds cost-oracle service module that runs workload replays against simplified execution models to estimate latency percentile and token/unit costs for candidate profiles. - Implements an autosuggest CLI: `redwood cost-oracle suggest --tenant <id> --dry-run` that emits JSON profile suggestions and a human-readable summary. - Adds a safeguards layer: suggested profiles are marked with risk levels (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH) and an enforceable fallback policy which will automatically revert to tenant baseline on observed latency regressions. - Introduces two new safe default libraries: compact-batching-presets and cautious-quant-profiles, plus mappings for common model families. - Adds telemetry events and a new trace tag (cost_oracle_run_id) so changes can be correlated with pre/post rollout metrics in Console. - Provides migration tooling to convert legacy tenant prefills into the new profile schema. - Includes curated unit tests, a small end-to-end integration test that runs the CLI against a synthetic trace, and docs/FAQ. Checklist: - [x] Simulator model implementation and unit tests - [x] CLI command and dry-run logic - [x] Safeguard/rollback hooks in runtime config apply path - [x] Migration script for legacy profiles - [x] Console docs and quickstart - [x] Telemetry/tracing hooks - [x] E2E smoke test on benchmark-lab Why this design: The offline simulator is intentionally conservative (models network/hardware variance as bounded percentiles) to avoid recommending aggressive quantization or large batch sizes that could push tail latency over SLOs. The autosuggest CLI is designed as an operator tool: suggestions are an opinionated starting point, not an automatic global policy. Backwards compatibility: Nothing changes unless an operator runs the CLI and applies a suggested profile or enables automated apply; the default runtime behavior and existing tenant profiles remain unchanged. Rollout plan: - Merge to main behind feature flag `feature.cost_oracle` - Deploy to staging and run benchmark-lab jobs for 48h - Share suggested profiles with 2 pilot tenants via SEs - Iterate on risk thresholds and telemetry mappings Implementation notes and high level commits: - simulator/: conservative latency/cost models and a small DSL for workload samples - cli/: cost-oracle CLI and JSON serializer for suggested profiles - runtime/apply/: guarded apply/rollback hooks integrated into profile applier - console-api/: REST surface for retrieving suggestions (read-only) - migrations/: legacy->profile schema converter - telemetry/: new event types and trace tags Tests: unit tests for simulator edges, integration smoke in benchmark-lab, added linting and type checks Documentation: - docs/ops/cost-oracle-quickstart.md - docs/ops/cost-oracle-faq.md Security & privacy: The simulator runs on replay data; no new customer data storage introduced. Telemetry uses existing tenant identifiers and respects PII redaction rules. Related work: builds on past autotune and prefiller components (see ENG-1244, ENG-1989) and complements the econ-advisor tools by offering a preflight simulation. Future work: add stochastic sampling of KV cache hit distributions, tighten model-family specific kernels, and UI to visualize tradeoffs.

+ def guarded_apply(profile, tenant):
+     snapshot = current_profile(tenant)
+     try:
+         apply(profile)
+         monitor_latency_and_rollback_if_violation()
